requirements.statement: Each router shall replay the active double-buffered calendar bank as 1,024 entries of {valid[0], in_port[2:0], out_port_mask[4:0], opcode[3:0]}. Calendar ID is 2 bits and an epoch bit selects the bank; only the inactive bank is writable and activation occurs atomically at slot 0 after old-epoch retirement.
requirements.resolution_rationale: A per-router table preserves offline conflict-free slot ownership and avoids per-hop route/header arbitration. Two 13-bit banks require only 26,624 bits per router.

rejected_alternatives.reason: Adds lookup/compare risk and cannot preserve explicit slot ownership without growing into a timetable.
Moves decisions into every flit, cannot reserve conflicting link slots, and increases header switching.

requirements.upstream_compliance: Implements REQ-F-001 replay semantics and retains the REQ-P-004 analytic table-depth assumption.
acceptance_criteria: A BFM replaying all valid entries selects exactly the encoded ingress, mask, and opcode.
The active bank is never written and no replay mixes entries from two epochs.
Total calendar storage per router is exactly 2 x 1,024 x 13 = 26,624 bits.

requirements.statement: Calendar replay shall use slot-owned zero-buffer forwarding, while BG and escape traffic use a dedicated credited XY-DOR class with one non-borrowable BG opportunity in every 16 slots. BG/demoted traffic may additionally use a calendar-idle output slot but never displaces a valid calendar transfer. An eligible one-flit request shall receive a per-hop grant within 16 slots and a longest-route delivery bound of 328 cycles after enqueue when downstream credit is available. The bound is T ≤ 2×RAMP + |dx|×(BG_WINDOW + T_router + H_LINK) + |dy|×(BG_WINDOW + T_router + V_LINK) with RAMP=1, BG_WINDOW=16, T_router=3, H_LINK=7, V_LINK=9; the credit return delays determine FIFO depth but are excluded by the downstream-credit eligibility premise. For the 12-hop 6×8 worst case (|dx|=5, |dy|=7) this equals 328 cycles.
requirements.resolution_rationale: Hybrid slots retain deterministic calendar replay while a periodic protected opportunity gives a finite BG service bound. X-before-Y ordering and release-before-demote prevent a cyclic cross-class dependency.

rejected_alternatives.candidate: dedicated calendar VC with strict priority
rejected_alternatives.reason: Dense calendar traffic can starve BG indefinitely.
Safe but leaves sparse calendar capacity unavailable and has worse flexibility/energy.

requirements.upstream_compliance: Provides the required mixed-traffic deadlock argument and concrete REQ-F-005 progress bound without changing the single 512-bit network.
acceptance_criteria: A mixed legal-calendar/BG BFM observes no cyclic wait and routes each BG packet X before Y.
Under continuous eligible demand and available downstream credit, each hop grants within 16 slots.
On a 12-hop route (|dx|=5, |dy|=7), a one-flit request completes within 328 cycles after enqueue using the stated link/router/ramp terms.

requirements.statement: Calendar payloads shall have no queued VC storage. BG/escape payload buffering shall use five per-input FIFOs of 20 flits each (100 flits, 51,200 bits per interior router), while per-egress credit counters enforce 16 flits for horizontal and 20 flits for vertical credit round trips; an egress transfer occurs only with available downstream credit.
requirements.resolution_rationale: Static calendar schedules do not need payload queues, while RTT-sized BG storage sustains a granted one-flit-per-cycle direction under H=7/V=9 delays.

rejected_alternatives.reason: Depth below the vertical 20-cycle return time creates avoidable full-rate bubbles and mixes traffic classes.
Adds allocator/storage area not needed for static calendar replay.

requirements.upstream_compliance: Meets REQ-F-008 no-overwrite behavior and REQ-P-001 rate under the stated analytic link timings.
acceptance_criteria: Credit counters never allow occupancy beyond allocated capacity.
A continuously granted H or V direction sustains one 512-bit flit per cycle after fill.
No legal backpressure test loses or duplicates a non-multicast flit.

requirements.statement: Trial 1 shall implement Tier-B two-input lane-wise combine for AND, OR, XOR, modulo-2^64 ADD, unsigned MIN, and unsigned MAX over eight 64-bit lanes with a calendar-reserved 3-cycle merge. IEEE floating point and unsupported operations shall use Tier-A PE compute. Tier-C DCA is disabled and only a future optional stub is retained.
requirements.resolution_rationale: Tier B has the selected +2.7% area class and the lowest evaluated allreduce cycles for m=1..5; DCA's 12-cycle visible latency and +16.9% class are not amortized.

rejected_alternatives.reason: Correct but has higher reduce/allreduce latency and PE energy; retained as fallback.
Requires unresolved FPU arbitration/format contracts and loses P1/P2 for 1–5 flit messages.

requirements.upstream_compliance: Satisfies the mandatory A/B/C comparison and preserves the optional nature of REQ-F-011.
acceptance_criteria: For each supported opcode, BFM output equals the defined lane-wise result and compiler-specified operand order.
Tier-B merge appears exactly three cycles after its reserved operand pair.
No DCA transaction is accepted when the Trial-1 configuration is selected.

requirements.statement: The router shall use a 32-cycle calendar watchdog after expected arrival and immediate early/wrong-port detection. A violation releases its calendar reservation exactly once, preserves the flit plus remaining 5-bit leaf mask, and emits one credited XY escape packet per unserved destination; recovery starts within two cycles when queue capacity is available.
requirements.resolution_rationale: Watchdog demotion provides bounded, observable lossless recovery without adding NACK/retry traffic or unbounded calendar resynchronization.

rejected_alternatives.candidate: per-slot validity/sequence check with immediate-only demotion
rejected_alternatives.reason: Does not bound a missing/blocked arrival.
Adds protocol state and can amplify congestion without improving the no-drop guarantee.

requirements.upstream_compliance: Meets REQ-F-006 atomic-fork accounting and REQ-F-009 graceful no-loss delivery for early, late, and wrong-port cases.
acceptance_criteria: BFM tests each early, late, and wrong-port case and observes eventual exactly-once delivery of every intended leaf.
A watchdog event produces one reservation release and one recovery action per unserved destination.
No accepted multicast branch is replayed and no unserved branch is dropped.
